features.title: closed verdict list pq / classic13 / classic12 / none / refused / unreachable / nomail / checking, NO 'unknown'
domain name and host detail sealed (AES-256-GCM, vault-wrapped key), only HMAC + closed words in clear
append-only SHA-256 hash-chained log + gapless head row + verify door
forced RLS on 3 tables + guard trigger (writes only through doors)
CHECK constraints tie verdict to evidence (pq needs TLS 1.3 + ML-KEM, classic13 no ML-KEM, failure no group)
read door for up to 50 domains in one call (the chips of one compose box)
posture + selftest (31 checks, rolls back) + CHECK_E189 (11 items)

Rust doors: GET /founder/v1/mail/tls (read only, kernel-verified) + POST /founder/v1/mail/tls/check (signed, asks for a probe: it is a write, so NOT a read-only door; correction of my earlier wording)
features.tech: Rust Tokio + rustls + rustls-post-quantum + hickory-resolver + axum

features.title: claim door: may this domain be probed now (atomic, advisory lock)
one probe per domain at a time, 24 h cache, 30 probes per mailbox per hour
Rust probe: DNS lookup + SMTP connect to the recipient MX from his server IP
EHLO mail.anexomail.com, STARTTLS, handshake, QUIT; never MAIL FROM
domain only, never an address (a test proves the address part is dropped)
named reason per host kept sealed in the detail (timeout, refused, no route)
retry schedule 1, 5, 30 minutes then stop with the reasons
due door: which unreachable domains are due, with the sealed name
Rust retry worker that claims, probes and finishes the due domains
the chip updates by itself (QLIVE signed tick, no refresh)
features.tech: Rust Tokio + QLIVE tick + React 19 TS

features.title: MX records sorted by priority (REUSES the existing fmail_smtp::targets + order_mx, no second copy)
no MX: the domain's A/AAAA is the implicit MX (RFC 5321 s5.1); exists in fmail_smtp::targets, the probe test proves it
null MX (RFC 7505) = nomail; exists in fmail_smtp::targets, the probe maps it to the nomail verdict
IPv4 and IPv6, every host tried
10 s connect and 10 s per command timeouts
handshake offers X25519MLKEM768 first, classic groups behind it
certificate verified yes/no recorded and shown, never hidden
all hosts listed with their own result (the verdict is the best-priority host that answered)
real-send door: a delivered mail records the real fact (rank 3)
a received mail is only a weak hint (rank 1), never replaces a probe or a real send
Rust hook: a delivered mail writes its TLS result into E189 (source sent); fmail_smtp Upgrade returns a TlsFact {verdict, group, version, cipher} instead of a bare word
Rust hook: a received mail writes a weak hint ONLY when the Postfix Received header proves TLS 1.2 or older or no TLS (a TLS 1.3 header names no group, so no pq / classic13 claim is made)
delivery proves or contradicts the prediction (proven_match / proven_mismatch ledger lines, mismatch flag)
Rust: at delivery the predicted verdict is compared and the mismatch line is written
UI addition: a 'proven' line on the sent mail
